title: Rust projects built with Cargo
description: For a Rust project built with Cargo: the declared minimum Rust version, compiler and Clippy warnings refused in CI, formatting checked, `unsafe` justified and bounded, and, for a service, a request path that returns errors instead of panicking. The last two rules concern a service that answers requests; a library or a command-line tool applies the others. Dependencies, the lockfile and RustSec advisories are in `rust-dependencies`. The Rust Style Guide is the reference behind the formatting rule, and `rustfmt` follows it by default.

sources.title: The Rust Programming Language, unsafe Rust
The Rust Programming Language, to panic! or not to panic!

rules.instruction: Declare `rust-version` in the `[package]` table of every crate the team publishes or deploys, or once in `[workspace.package]` for the members to inherit, and build with a toolchain of that version in CI so that the declared minimum is one the project verifies.
rules.verification: Check that each such crate states `rust-version` or inherits it, and that a CI job builds with a toolchain of that version (the Cargo Book's CI guide shows one with `cargo hack check --rust-version`); on an older toolchain `cargo check` stops with Cargo's error.

rules.instruction: Run `cargo clippy` on all targets and features in CI and fail the job on any lint warning, from the compiler or from Clippy: set `build.warnings = "deny"` (or the `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS` variable) where the project's Cargo supports it, otherwise pass `-D warnings` to Clippy. Pin the toolchain the job runs, since warnings carry few compatibility guarantees between releases.
rules.verification: On a scratch branch, add an unused variable and check that the CI job fails; check that the job names the toolchain version it runs and that a change of that version goes through a pull request.

rules.instruction: Check formatting in CI with `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, so that the build fails on code rustfmt would change, and commit a `rustfmt.toml` only for the options the team changes from the default style.
rules.verification: On a scratch branch, break the formatting of one file and check that the CI formatting job exits with a non-zero status; if `rustfmt.toml` exists, check that it lists only options the team chose on purpose.

rules.instruction: Put a `// SAFETY:` comment on every `unsafe` block and impl, saying how the safety rules are upheld, and a `# Safety` section in the documentation of every public `unsafe fn`, saying what its caller must ensure. Deny `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` and `clippy::missing_safety_doc` in the crates that contain `unsafe`.
rules.verification: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` with the two lints at deny and check that it exits with status 0; read each `unsafe` the change adds against its comment.

rules.instruction: State the `unsafe` policy of each crate in its lints: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` in `[lints.rust]` for a crate that needs none; for one that does, set it to `deny` and allow it only in one small module that exposes a safe API, with each `unsafe` block as small as it can be.
rules.verification: Check the `[lints.rust]` table (or `[workspace.lints.rust]`) of each crate, search the crate for `unsafe` and check that every hit sits in the one allowed module, and run the tests of that module under Miri (`cargo +nightly miri test`), which the Rust Book recommends for unsafe code.

rules.instruction: In a service, make every handler and every function it calls on request data return a `Result` whose error becomes an HTTP response with the right status (`IntoResponse` in axum, `ResponseError` in Actix Web), so that a malformed or hostile request never reaches `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or an index that can panic. Where an `expect` stays, outside the request path, give it a message that states why the failure cannot happen.
rules.verification: For each route the change touches, send a malformed body, a missing field and an out-of-range value in a test and assert a 4xx response, with no 500 and no dropped connection; if a catch-panic layer is installed (tower-http's `CatchPanic` answers a panic with a 500), check that these tests also pass without it.

rules.instruction: In the crates of a service, deny `clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::expect_used` and `clippy::panic` in `[lints.clippy]` (or `[workspace.lints.clippy]`), and keep them allowed in tests with `allow-unwrap-in-tests`, `allow-expect-in-tests` and `allow-panic-in-tests` in `clippy.toml`. Write a comment that justifies each `#[allow]` of these lints in the service code.
rules.verification: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and check that it exits with status 0, then search the service code for `allow(clippy::unwrap_used`, `allow(clippy::expect_used` and `allow(clippy::panic` and check that each hit has a comment.
